samples.summary: Recording authorship is gated on the same opt-in as *displaying* it, which is not in the issue's design and materially weakens acceptance criterion 1 ("each line shows the author of its most recent edit")
samples.evidence: The todo/issue design (docs/tasks/active/20260822-notes-blame-gutter-todo.md:30-33) says the Yorkie store should "write the attributes on insert (author read from the local presence `name`…)" — unconditionally. The diff instead adds `YorkieNoteStoreOptions.recordAuthorship` (default false) and wires it to the display preference `wafflebase:notes:showAuthors` (notes-detail.tsx / notes-view.tsx). Consequence: a user who turns the gutter ON still sees blank labels for every line written by collaborators who never turned it on — which for most notes is every line. The feature's headline criterion is only satisfied among the subset of users who opted in. The rationale is documented in docs/design/notes/notes.md, but it is a behavioural deviation from the specified design and should be an explicit product decision, not an implementation choice folded into the PR.

samples.summary: The anonymous share-link editing path never enables authorship recording or the gutter, so acceptance criterion "anonymous lines fall back to 'Anonymous'" is unreachable in the shipped product
samples.evidence: `shared-document.tsx:345` mounts `<NotesView readOnly={readOnly} viewMode={readOnly ? "view" : "both"} />` with no `showAuthors` prop, so `recordAuthorship` stays false for exactly the anonymous share-link editors whose presence name is `"Anonymous"`. The only mount that ever enables recording is the authenticated `notes-detail.tsx`. The "Anonymous" fallback (`ANONYMOUS_AUTHOR` in blame-gutter.ts) is therefore only exercised by tests and by the empty-presence edge case, not by the anonymous-editing scenario the issue names. Anonymous share-link viewers also have no way to turn the gutter on (no view menu on that surface).

samples.summary: Peer-caret color/name hardening (`sanitizePeerColor`, `FALLBACK_PEER_COLOR`, caret-name sanitization) is unrequested scope in a blame-gutter PR
samples.evidence: Issue #814's acceptance criteria are entirely about the per-line author gutter. `sanitizePeerColor()` and its tests fix a pre-existing style-attribute injection in the remote-selection caret, a code path this feature does not introduce or touch functionally. Reusing `sanitizeDisplayName` for the caret label is arguably in-family; refusing peer colors is a separate defect fix that belongs in its own change (and its own issue), where it can be reviewed and released on its own merits rather than riding a feature branch.

samples.summary: `sanitizeDisplayName` is placed in `@wafflebase/notes` although it is a cross-engine concern (docs/slides also render self-reported peer names)
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/peer-cursor.ts` renders peer presence names too, and shared cross-engine helpers in this repo live in `@wafflebase/core` (no equivalent exists there — grepped `packages/core` for `sanitize`/`displayName`, no matches). Putting the only display-name sanitizer inside the notes engine means the next engine that needs it either re-implements it or takes an inappropriate dependency on notes. Not blocking, but core is the layer this belongs in.
searchedFor: grep presence/peer name usage in packages/docs/src

samples.summary: Blame-gutter internals are exported from the package's public API without a consumer
samples.evidence: `ANONYMOUS_AUTHOR`, `computeBlameLabels`, `noteBlameGutter` and `noteBlameTracker` are re-exported from `packages/notes/src/index.ts`, but the host only ever uses the editor API (`NoteEditorOptions.showAuthors`, `setShowAuthors`) — the extensions are wired internally by `editor.ts`. Exporting the extensions and the label algorithm widens the engine's public surface for test convenience.

verdict.reason: Verified present as described: `YorkieNoteStoreOptions.recordAuthorship` (yorkie-note-store.ts:65-68) defaults to false (:149) and gates the attribute write in editText (:186-196); it is bound to the *display* preference `wafflebase:notes:showAuthors` in notes-view.tsx:121 and :167-169 via notes-detail.tsx:47,203,210 / notes-settings.ts:11. The todo's design (docs/tasks/active/20260822-notes-blame-gutter-todo.md:30-33) specifies writing the attributes on insert with no such condition, and acceptance criterion 1 (:9-10) is "each line shows the author of its most recent edit"; the blank-label allowance (:14-16) is scoped only to pre-feature text, not to lines written by peers who never opted in. So the coupling is a real, in-lane spec deviation that can leave most lines blank even for a user who turns the gutter on. The design doc does record the rationale (docs/design/notes/notes.md:512-533) and the todo intro (:5, "Nothing changes for someone who never turns it on") arguably supports it, but that reading is about the opted-out user's own view/layout (criterion 3, :12-13), not about suppressing their contribution to others' gutters — ambiguous, not refuting. No guard makes recording unconditional (notes-view.tsx:88 even defaults showAuthors=false for the share-link mount). Nothing to refute on; finding stays.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `SharedNotesLayout` (shared-document.tsx:322-349) mounts `<NotesView readOnly viewMode>` at line 345 with no `showAuthors`, and renders no `NotesToolbar`/view menu on that surface. `notes-view.tsx:88` defaults `showAuthors` to false, and that single flag gates BOTH `new YorkieNoteStore(doc, { recordAuthorship: showAuthors })` (line 121) and `initialize(..., { showAuthors })` (line 124), so anonymous share-link editors neither record nor see authorship. A repo-wide grep finds exactly two `NotesView` mounts (notes-detail.tsx:207 — the only one passing `showAuthors`, line 210 — and shared-document.tsx:345) and one `NotesToolbar` usage (notes-detail.tsx:198); `notes-settings.ts` is prop-fed and explicitly not used by the shared surface, so there is no indirect path. The presence name IS `"Anonymous"` for these visitors (shared-document.tsx:838, 887-893), but `YorkieNoteStore.editText` only writes the `a` attribute when `recordAuthorship` is true (yorkie-note-store.ts:186), so an anonymous editor's lines stay unattributed. The `ANONYMOUS_AUTHOR` fallback (blame-gutter.ts:24,57) fires only on an empty author string, and notes-detail.tsx:246 blocks mounting for users without a username, so in production it is reachable only via the empty-presence edge case — not the anonymous-editing scenario the issue's acceptance criterion names ("Anonymous editing keeps working; anonymous lines fall back to 'Anonymous'", docs/tasks/active/20260822-notes-blame-gutter-todo.md:17-18) and that the design doc asserts (docs/design/notes/notes.md:555-558). No counterexample found after searching all mounts, the settings module, the provider wiring, and the design docs.
